mission: Use object-level museum provenance, dealer archives, acquisition files and export documentation to test whether the early twentieth-century Nahman dealer network intersects multiple Osirian object classes and whether any such intersection can lawfully backlink to the unresolved Mendes 1902 stamped-gold djed or other missing-member evidence.

nodes.document: May 1904 consular certificate in Bowdoin accession file
nodes.firewall: This proves a dealer/export node for one shabti from the burial, not a route for CG53469 or the stamped-gold djed.

nodes.interpretation: Strong Osirian reliquary/dealer node. The object title/type does not by itself prove archaeological findspot at Abydos or that any biological material was contained in this specific object.

nodes.finding: The Met states that in later periods the Abydos emblem was viewed as the reliquary containing the head of Osiris.
nodes.firewall: A type-level head-reliquary tradition does not establish content in Louvre E11072.
Material, date and provenance do not identify this with Quibell's stamped-gold Mendes djed.

nodes.collection: Maurice Nahman, Antiquaire. Visitor book and miscellaneous papers. 1909-2006
nodes.target: business-name variants, early invoices/ledgers/letterheads, stock numbers, export papers and referrals capable of testing Nahman & Co. identity

dealer_infrastructure_control.finding: Published research documents Maurice Nahman stock/inventory numbers and a surviving ledger reference, and notes Griffith Institute Clere dealer files with photographs/notes of objects seen in Nahman's shop.
dealer_infrastructure_control.implication: Object-level dealer backtracing is technically plausible where ledger numbers, photographs, invoices or acquisition records survive.
dealer_infrastructure_control.chronology_firewall: Later documented ledger practice may guide the search but must not be projected backward onto 1904 without primary evidence.

new_primary_requests.target: Louvre, Département des Antiquités égyptiennes documentation
new_primary_requests.request: E11072 acquisition/object dossier: exact seller wording, invoice/stock/shipment identifiers, archaeological provenance, prior ownership, cavity/content/opening/restoration/scientific examination, early photographs and batch-acquisition context
Maurice Nahman records: test Nahman & Co. identity, pre-1910 business names/letterheads/invoices/ledgers/stock numbers/export papers and Mendes/Abydos/Osiris/djed references
Scan/photo of May 1904 consular certificate for 1905.25.2 preserving literal dealer name, address, seals, consignor/consignee, shipment/box/invoice fields and company wording

missing_member_search_reframe.rule: Search for documented containers, reliquaries, mummy equipment, accession passports and custody chains before treating mythic place-name lists as physical-location evidence.

priority_lanes.physical_candidate_class: gold phallus sheath / protected body-gold equipment

priority_lanes.textual_node: Athribis/Letopolis/Heracleopolis and other late relic-geography traditions
priority_lanes.physical_candidate_class: sealed chests, reliquaries, ritual substitutes, mummy equipment, excavated deposits

strong_pass_condition: Recover primary documentation tying the Bowdoin 1904 wording 'Nahman & Co.' to Maurice Nahman or his business, then recover object-level shipment/stock/invoice or acquisition evidence that intersects a Mendes 1902 gold-object group, the unresolved stamped-gold djed, or another independently attested Osirian member-container context.
next_actions: Wait for Bowdoin certificate image and transcribe literally before normalizing dealer identity.
Wait for Louvre E11072 dossier and distinguish archaeological provenance from Osirian typology.
Wait for Brooklyn archive guidance/scans and search any returned business-name variants against 1904-1905 records.
Build a source-ranked corpus of physical reliquaries/containers for other Osiris member traditions, prioritizing archaeological context and museum accession records over late mythic geography alone.
Cross-link only object-level dealer or shipment identifiers back into JdE VI 486-487 / Engelbach / CG53465-53475.
canonical_formula: MENDES_1904_NAHMAN_AND_CO + LOUVRE_1905_MAURICE_NAHMAN_OSIRIAN_RELIQUARY + BM_1909_MAURICE_NAHMAN_DJED => HIGH_PRIORITY_DEALER_IDENTITY_AND_LEDGER_TEST; NOT A RELIC IDENTIFICATION
canonical_seal: THE NEW CLUE IS NOT THAT NAHMAN OWNED OSIRIS. THE CLUE IS THAT A DOCUMENTED DEALER NETWORK TOUCHES MULTIPLE OSIRIAN OBJECT CLASSES. FOLLOW THE INVOICES UNTIL THE OBJECTS SEPARATE OR JOIN.
